rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Batch and continuous are the two architectures of chemical production: a recipe followed in time versus an equilibrium held in space. Batch wins flexibility, low capital, and validation-friendly lots (pharma, food, dyes); continuous wins scale economics, consistency and low labour (ammonia, acids, petrochemicals) — because high fixed costs demand unbroken tonnage.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Batch: output per year = lot size × lots per year (limited by cleaning/changeover time) - Continuous: output per year = rate × 8760 h × availability factor

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: continuous, batch processing (within Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Process choice is an economic variable - the volume and the customer, not the reaction, pick the architecture.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The same reaction, two architectures*** - esterification at kilo scale in a flavour house (batch) and at tonne scale in biodiesel (continuous) - chemistry identical, economics decides.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Batch versus Continuous Processing Every chemical plant answers one architectural question first: **make the product in discrete batches, or run the process continuously without stopping?** Batch processing makes a defined quantity, cleans, and repeats; continuous processing feeds raw material and draws product in unbroken streams at steady state.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Batch processing:** charge the reactor → process for a set time → discharge → clean → repeat. Output is in lots; composition varies during the batch. Suited to: small volumes, multiple products in one vessel, pharma, food, dyes, specialty chemicals.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Batch control is a recipe; continuous control is an equilibrium - the knowledge lives in documents vs instruments.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Batch: charge -> process -> discharge -> clean -> repeat; recipe-controlled; flexible, labour-heavy, low capital; pharma/food/dyes/specialty. Continuous: unbroken feed and product at steady state; instrument-loop-controlled; capital-heavy, labour-light, consistent, scale-economical; petrochemicals/ammonia/acids.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ammonia plants run 350+ days a year - every idle day is fixed-cost spread lost.

rows.text: Explain why slow addition of one reagent (semi-batch) controls an exotherm.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Continuous is always more modern":** it is more *economic at scale* — for pharma, batch remains the right answer for validation and flexibility reasons. **"Batch plants have no instrumentation":** they have plenty — but their control variable is time, not steady-state position.
